reference_drawer.title: 📖 Tangents from an External Point Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Essential theorems and geometric facts for external tangents.

items.rule: Tangents from the same external point to a circle are equal.
items.example: Use equality before forming a linear equation.

items.rule: At each vertex, the two tangent segments to the circle are equal.
items.example: Hence the triangle perimeter is twice the sum of the three vertex tangent lengths.

items.rule: The sums of opposite sides of a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle are equal.
items.example: Use this relation to find an unknown side or verify a result.

items.rule: Use the specified tangent-secant relation for AP.
items.example: First compute the full perimeter of triangle CDE, then take one-half.
